card.title: Manufacture of sodium carbonate by ammonia soda or Solvay…

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The Solvay process turns brine and limestone into sodium carbonate with ammonia as the reusable scaffold: carbonation gives NH₄HCO₃, solubility selects NaHCO₃ alone to precipitate, calcination yields the soda and returns the CO₂, and lime closes the ammonia loop — leaving the net equation 2NaCl + CaCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + CaCl₂ with ammonia absent.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - NH₃ + CO₂ + H₂O → NH₄HCO₃; NH₄HCO₃ + NaCl → NaHCO₃↓ + NH₄Cl - 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂; 2NH₄Cl + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCl₂ + 2NH₃ + 2H₂O - Net: 2NaCl + CaCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + CaCl₂

rows.text: Ammonia is the process's reusable scaffold, not its fuel.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Stoichiometric en route, catalytic overall*** - ammonia enters every step's equation yet vanishes from the net reaction - a reagent with a catalyst's economics.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Sodium Carbonate by the Ammonia–Soda (Solvay) Process The Solvay process makes sodium carbonate from three cheap inputs — **brine, limestone and ammonia** — with the ammonia recycled as a carrier: NH₃ absorbs CO₂ to give ammonium bicarbonate, which metathesises with NaCl to precipitate the sparingly soluble NaHCO₃, calcined to Na₂CO₃.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Inputs:** brine (NaCl), limestone (CaCO₃), ammonia (recycled), water; fuel for calcination. - **Step 1 — ammoniation and carbonation:** NH₃ + CO₂ + H₂O → NH₄HCO₃ (ammoniated brine absorbs CO₂ from the kiln gas). - **Step 2 — precipitation:** NH₄HCO₃ + NaCl → NaHCO₃↓ + NH₄Cl — sodium bicarbonate's **low solubility** in the cold ammoniated brine makes it the only solid that crashes out.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Four equations + the net reaction with ammonia cancelled - the net equation proves the carrier claim.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Solubility, not reactivity, does the selecting - the process only makes the wanted salt the least soluble thing present.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Inputs: brine, limestone, recycled ammonia. Steps: (1) NH3 + CO2 + H2O -> NH4HCO3 in ammoniated brine; (2) NH4HCO3 + NaCl -> NaHCO3(s) + NH4Cl - selective by low solubility; (3) 2NaHCO3 -> Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2 (CO2 recycled); (4) 2NH4Cl + Ca(OH)2 -> CaCl2 + 2NH3 + 2H2O (ammonia recovered; lime from CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A process's by-product, not its product, often decides its survival - the Leblanc process died of waste; Solvay lives with CaCl2.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Ammonia as a Carrier: The Process's Masterstroke - Ammonia's role is **provisional basicity:** it raises the brine's effective carbonate concentration by holding CO₂ as NH₄HCO₃, creating the conditions in which NaHCO₃ precipitates — then it is *recovered and returned*.…  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — Why NaHCO3 Precipitates: Solubility as Selectivity - The carbonating tower's brine contains Na⁺, NH₄⁺, Cl⁻ and HCO₃⁻ — four salts are possible; **only NaHCO₃ is sparingly soluble** in the cold concentrated solution (NaCl, NH₄Cl, NH₄HCO₃ all stay dissolved).…  ·  ### Deep dive — Solvay: ammonia as a recyclable carrier of CO₂ Brine (NaCl) + limestone (CaCO₃) + ammonia produce NaHCO₃, which calcines to Na₂CO₃. The elegant part is the **ammonia cycle**: NH₃ is absorbed in brine, CO₂ (from CaCO₃ calcination) precipitates NaHCO₃ because it is the least soluble thing in the four-ion system, and NH₃ is recovered from the mother liquor by…

rows.text: ## 6.
